chokhmat-shlomo/part-001.txt.1:_: Seif 1 — The waiter who ate a kezayit—they invite zimun on him. In my humble opinion: behold in the Talmud they ask it is obvious and answer lest you say he did not fix [a place], etc. Behold in my composition Sefer HaChaim siman 486 I raised that even for prohibition food between the teeth does not combine and we require a kezayit outside the teeth; nevertheless for a mitzvah, even between the teeth combines from the power of achshaveh—for the mitzvah considers it [as eating] and he wants it to be eating—therefore even between the teeth combines [and there in Sefer HaChaim I did not write from the power of achshaveh but in my chiddushim to Mechaber I wrote thus and compared this to what Beit Yosef wrote in Shulchan Aruch Orach Chayim siman 31: if it is worth in one place it helps for me; if it is not worth in any place it does not help for me. So one may say similarly regarding kezayit: when it is a kezayit, then when lacking between the teeth, since before he ate it was a kezayit, achshaveh helps; but if it is less than a kezayit literally, achshaveh does not help; and for prohibition achshaveh is not applicable for he does not want to become obligated—and on the contrary one may say he ate knowing it was not a kezayit except between the teeth and he will be exempt, therefore achshaveh is not applicable]. And behold one should examine in birkat hamazon what its law is: shall we say since in birkat hamazon it is a mitzvah, it also combines between the teeth; or since there is no obligation to bless lest it be annulled and not blessed, the eating itself is reshut and what is between the teeth does not combine. And apparently it would be proven from here—for what does the Talmud ask it is obvious; shall we say it teaches us that even if he ate only with between the teeth it also combines, and it would be proven from this that it does not combine. However from this there is no proof, for it cannot answer thus—for if so it is difficult why specifically a waiter did it mention; behold this applies to every person; therefore it must answer lest you say he did not fix. But this may prove from what it asks afterward: and the waiter who ate less than a kezayit—it is obvious—and answers since, etc.; and what does it ask; shall we say for at first it said therefore it mentioned waiter, for one would think he did not fix and that is he has no intent to combine. And according to this it teaches that even though he did not fix he still combines; nevertheless one may say thus: this is the distinction—that in any case in him we require a kezayit outside the teeth; therefore it teaches the waiter who ate less than a kezayit—meaning with between the teeth it is a kezayit only if what between the teeth is not combined it is only less than a kezayit; and it teaches that in another person it combines even between the teeth for birkat hamazon—meaning since he fixed we testify that at the time of eating his intent was to combine and bless birkat hamazon and his intent was to be considered eating even with between the teeth; but in a waiter who did not fix, at the time of eating it did not enter his mind to combine—therefore he did not consider it eating even for the teeth; and therefore since he did not consider it at eating time to combine also between the teeth, again it is less than a kezayit and they do not invite zimun on him. And it teaches much: and what does it ask it is obvious; and why should I force and say since; and perforce it is proven that in birkat hamazon even in every person we require outside the teeth; and if so it is difficult why specifically waiter; therefore it answers since—and examine well, for it is correct.
chokhmat-shlomo/part-001.txt.2:_: There seif 3 — A gentile they do not invite zimun on him; and even a convert who was circumcised and did not immerse they do not invite zimun on him. In my humble opinion: see in Magen Avraham what he wrote—all who did not immerse properly, as written in Yoreh Deah siman 124 seif 2. And in my humble opinion there is no proof—for granted there it is for stringency, therefore all who did not immerse properly make yayin nesech; but here since from the Torah he is obligated in zimun, even though from the Sages it is not immersion—nevertheless since from the Torah he is a convert and from the Torah they are obligated in birkat hamazon, they combine; and he is no worse in this than a Cuthean whom they invite zimun on him—and that is such as if he did not immerse before three, as explicit in Yoreh Deah siman 268—for the Rif and Rambam he is invalid; nevertheless since it is only d'rabbanan—for they agree his sons are fit as written there—and the matter is necessary for them from the body of the Talmud that says R' Yehuda: circumcised and did not immerse as if he did not circumcise; and why does it not teach us that even (not) immersed—only that he is not a convert before three; and behold if he did not immerse he is not before three—and it should teach us extra greatness that even immersed not before three he is not a convert. And perforce it is proven that even for them it is only d'rabbanan; and R' Yehuda teaches us that not immersed at all is as if he did not circumcise and is not a convert from the Torah; but if he immersed not before three he is a convert from the Torah, only from the Sages he is not a convert—therefore they combine him for zimun. And proof from what it answers in Berachot—for it asks there and the gentile is obvious—and answers a convert circumcised and did not immerse as Reish Lakish said: a convert circumcised and did not immerse is as if he did not circumcise; and it is difficult here—it should have taught us greatness and said even if he immersed only that he did not immerse properly likewise they do not invite zimun on him—why did it answer that he did not immerse at all. And perforce it is proven that if he immersed, even if not properly, they invite zimun on him—and not like Magen Avraham—and examine well.

dagul-merevavah/part-001.txt.1:_: Meaning: for the berachah of zimun they do not understand; but for birkat hamazon they must understand.

eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.1:_: [1] Cuthean, etc. One who is wicked publicly and transgresses sins—and all the more a mumar to idolatry—they do not invite zimun on him.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.2:_: [2] Am ha'aretz complete, etc. It implies even if he does not recite Keriat Shema morning and evening; and so wrote Kenesset HaGedolah; and Olat Tamid and Magen Avraham wrote they do not invite zimun on him—for it is not applicable that each build a bamah for himself, since most amei ha'aretz recite Keriat Shema; and for an individual we do not care.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.3:_: [3] [Levush] And even with her husband, etc. Malbushei Yom Tov wrote this is his language: he wrote in derashot of Maharash that he ate with his wife and called one to drink with him to invite zimun with him and told him he fulfills the final blessing on wine in the berachah of ha-Zan that he heard; and this zimun with his wife is difficult for me—for Rabbeinu Yonah wrote even with their husbands not, because their company is not fitting—until here his language. And I did not know what was difficult for him—for it seems to him like what Tur wrote in the name of R' Yehuda Kohen who ruled halacha lema'aseh to combine a woman for zimun and brought proof from that the Talmud requires [clarification whether] women in birkat hamazon are d'oraisa or d'rabbanan, and he said what practical difference—to discharge others' obligation—for it is obvious to him they combine; for if you do not say so, when it requires whether they can discharge, it should require whether they combine—until here. And incidentally let us say in it a matter—that Bach wrote on Tur's words mentioned above: you might say a great wonder—for we taught explicitly women, slaves, and minors they do not invite zimun on them; and it appears he did not rule except to combine for ten and not for three, and so we conclude—until here. And it escaped me the responsum of Maharam of Rothenburg siman 227 who wrote explicitly she can combine even for three; and so wrote in Agur siman 249; and aside from this you might say on him that if he admits it is forbidden to combine for three—if so still difficult—it should require whether they combine for three. And the main wonder that Bach wondered—one may say R' Yehuda Kohen holds with her husband it is permitted and through this he permitted; and I saw in Derishah who answered that it seems to him the Mishnah says thus: women, slaves, and minors in combinations together do not combine because of promiscuity of slaves with women, and slaves with minors because of homosexuality—until here his language. And I wonder—for if so what does the Talmud daf 47 ask from the Mishnah on R' Yosi who said a minor lying in a cradle—they invite zimun on him—for R' Yosi deals not with combination of women and slaves together but with free males. I still have wonder on Bach who interprets Maharam of Rothenburg's words that Tur wrote ha in the responsum mentioned above explicit to the contrary—see there, for I shortened since it does not affect our law—for I wrote above we practice not to combine a woman at all even for ten; and even though Bach ruled to combine a woman or slave for ten for mention of the Name—I never saw practiced thus; and so wrote Agur siman 244.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.4:_: [4] [Levush] That birkat hamazon requires, etc. It appears he answers thus the wonder of Lechem Chamudot daf 56—that Rama's words here and in siman 193 contradict—for there he wrote they must understand; see there. And it appears to me Levush holds to distinguish that even in berachat zimun they need not understand; nevertheless birkat hamazon requires understanding; and so explained Nachalat Tzvi Rama's words; however one must give a reason to distinguish between them; and perhaps because we rely on poskim that it seems to him women are never obligated only reshut; and since there is no obligation he ruled like Rashi and R' Yitzchak that even if they do not understand they fulfill. One may also say it seems to Rama like Kenesset HaGedolah siman 62 and Olat Tamid siman 193 in the name of Birkat Avraham—that specifically an individual discharges an individual; but an individual who discharges many such as zimun with three and one discharges two—and all the more if they are ten in zimun with the Name; and similarly in a shaliach tzibur who discharges many in his prayer—their obligation for everyone—even if they do not understand they fulfill—until here; therefore here in zimun women fulfill; and in siman 193 it deals when there is no zimun. Only from Levush it implies even when they bless in zimun with three they do not fulfill in birkat hamazon when they do not understand—for it refers to zimun and wrote and I already wrote, etc.; I also examined Sefer Birkat Avraham itself daf 247 who wrote that women for zimun since they do not combine they are like an individual discharging an individual; and see above siman 193 s.k. 2—I wrote to practice the law; therefore I shortened.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.5:_: [5] [Levush] It is from the Torah, etc. And the view of Olat Tamid is it is d'rabbanan and the verse is merely an asmachta; and an androgynous is not obligated but reshut to invite zimun with his kind; and so implies Tosafot Berachot daf 46 s.v. ad, etc.; and so wrote in Sefer Keriat Sefar; however zimun with ten who mention the Name he wrote is d'oraisa and berachat et Hashem Elokecha—and requires study; and see below siman 589 and siman 689. Levush omitted the law of slaves; and in Tur and Shulchan Aruch it wrote women and slaves they do not invite zimun on them; and one must say Levush relies on the rule that whatever a woman is commanded a slave is commanded. Olat Tamid wrote and it appears from what it teaches slaves and does not teach free men—it implies half-slave half-free they invite zimun on him—and that is the reason since they force his master to make him a free man he is as if already a free man—and requires study for practice—until here his language. And he wanted to say it should have taught they invite zimun only on a free man—and easy to understand. And it is difficult—for below siman 589 regarding shofar and siman 689 regarding Megillah we hold even for himself one does not discharge who is half-slave half-free. And further difficult—for above siman 143 it wrote on what Shulchan Aruch wrote they do not read Torah with fewer than ten free men—and this is his language—to exclude complete slaves and half-slave half-free—it appears he is obligated—until here his language; behold his words contradict. Also above he ruled like stam and here he left for practice in requires study—and above it was explained for law that certainly the aspect of slavery exists on him. And nevertheless here it is possible they invite zimun on him since the reason is promiscuity—and since he is half-free and they force his master there is not so much promiscuity. Also from Talmud Chagigah daf 4 it implies where it taught slaves stam it implies completely—for if not let it teach slaves who are not freed; and it is possible to align thus Olat Tamid's words—and examine well; and see Rokeach siman 343, and in Sifrei Yoreh Deah siman 1.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.6:_: [6] [Levush] And presumably, etc. Specifically they do not combine; but to discharge others we require we know certainly he brought two hairs—for birkat hamazon is d'oraisa; so wrote Magen Avraham—not like Rashal and Bach; and see above siman 55. And it appears that which they practice to give to bless a thirteen-year-old boy stam—that is they practice also each to bless by himself silently; and see below siman 225 s.k. 4.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.7:_: [7] Deaf and fool, etc. Meaning: deaf-mute who speaks and does not hear; but if he does not hear and does not speak he does not combine, as above siman 55 seif 8; and so wrote in Lechem Chamudot. And likewise it does not deal with the fool the Sages spoke of as explained in Yoreh Deah siman 1, but a fool who is not wise and the public hold him as a fool; and in Eliyah Rabbah to Yoreh Deah it will be explained at length.
eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.8:_: [8] See in Yoreh Deah siman 334. And above siman 55 seif 12.

kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.1:_: (1) [Seif 1] The waiter who ate, etc.—lest you say he has no fixed [eating], for he goes and comes—it teaches us Berachot 47 folio 2, Beit Yosef there s.k. 1. And even though he does not fix a place for a meal—for behold he must go here and there—nevertheless since his way is thus, this is his fixing. Levush ot 1; however Petaḥ HaDe'ah in siman 197 wrote this law does not apply to the waiter practiced among us—for the reason the waiter combines even though he did not fix is because his way of eating is thus—and that was the waiter's way: to wash hands and bless ha-Motzi and stand to serve the reclining ones; but the waiter nowadays this is not his way of eating—to eat from the table of the reclining ones but afterward reclines at his table like everyone in the land; and there is no way to give him something from the table as in Talmudic times; and similarly Shlah daf 62; and if so his law returns like any other person—as the Rosh wrote another person who eats like the waiter would not combine since he has no fixity—see there. And they brought Shadich Asad ma'arechet 7 ot 8; and therefore one should follow local custom: if they practice like Talmudic times he combines even without fixing; if they practice like Petaḥ HaDe'ah he does not combine until he fixes with them.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.2:_: (2) [Seif 2] Cuthean nowadays, etc.—and Cutheans are those Sennacherib settled in cities of Samaria as written the king of Assyria came from Babylon and Cutah, etc.; and because he brought them from Cutah they are called Cutheans; and they converted from fear of lions as written Hashem sent among them lions, etc.—Rashi Kiddushin 75 folio 1. And afterward he made them actual gentiles as stated in Chullin 6 folio 1; and see Beit Yosef.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.3:_: (3) There Cuthean nowadays, etc.—and even if he is a chaver; but a Sadducee they invite zimun on him if he is a chaver. Razah ot 2; however see Shach Yoreh Deah siman 2 s.k. 24 who wrote in the name of responsum R' Betzalel siman 3 that this deals with Sadducee and Boethusian in former times when they had some good measures; but in these Karaites nowadays who corrupted their deeds—behold they are like gentiles—see there. And so Zivchei Tzedek likewise in the name of several poskim—see there. And therefore also for zimun one should be stringent; and see in the ot afterward.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.4:_: (4) There Cuthean nowadays, etc.—and likewise Karaites do not complete a minyan and do not combine for Kaddish and prayer and zimun—Rambam in responsa Pe'er HaDor siman 41; Beit Yosef Mechaber ot 3; and so above siman 55 ot 63—see there.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.5:_: (5) There. Cuthean nowadays, etc.—and it is obvious that one wicked publicly transgressing sins—and all the more a mumar—they do not invite zimun on him, for he is no worse than am ha'aretz in Talmudic times—Magen Avraham s.k. 2; Eliyah Rabbah ot 2; Shulchan Gavoah ot 1; Yad Ephraim in Hagahat Turei Zahav; Razah ot 3—and that is one who transgresses many sins; for from one sin specifically they excommunicated him; but if they did not excommunicate him he combines as in seif 11—Avnei Nezer ot 2; and see above siman 55 seif 11 and in our words there ot 16.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.6:_: (6) [Seif 3] Am ha'aretz complete, etc.—meaning that in the Gemara Berachot 47 folio 2 they say that even if he read and learned and did not serve Torah scholars to understand reasons of mishnayot—they do not invite zimun on him; except that Tosafot and Rosh there wrote that nowadays they invite zimun on am ha'aretz so each should not go and build a bamah for himself—see there; and so Tur; and such are Shulchan Aruch's words.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.7:_: (7) There am ha'aretz complete, etc.—it implies even if he does not know to recite Keriat Shema morning and evening they invite zimun on him nowadays. However Sefer HaGuf part 3 she'achlu wrote in the name of Riaz that if he does not recite Keriat Shema morning and evening—even nowadays they do not invite zimun on him—see there. And they brought it like Hagahat Turei Zahav; Olat Torah ot 2; and Magen Avraham s.k. 1 wrote it is not applicable here that each build a bamah for himself since most am ha'aretz recite Keriat Shema; and for an individual we do not care—see there. Eliyah Rabbah ot 2; Razah ot 3; Beit Yosef Mechaber ot 5; Kitzur Shulchan Aruch siman 45 ot 23.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.8:_: (8) [Seif 4] A gentile they do not invite zimun on him. And in the Gemara it is obvious—the question is a convert in Eretz Yisrael circumcised and did not immerse—Bach. And even if he intended to bless our God they do not invite zimun on him—Razah ot 4.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.9:_: (9) There and even a convert circumcised and did not immerse, etc.—and whenever he did not immerse properly he is called did not immerse, as written in Yoreh Deah siman 124 seif 2 Magen Avraham s.k. 2; and if he immersed before circumcision it is a doubt as written in Yoreh Deah siman 268 seif 1; and tumtum requires study whether to compare him to one whose foreskin was removed—the verse stated in Yoreh Deah there or not; and behold it is obvious in birkat hamazon a Torah doubt is for stringency and a doubt does not remove from certainty—Avnei Nezer ot 2; and an Israelite mumar who repented—see responsa 11—that he requires immersion as written in Yoreh Deah siman 267 seif 8 and in siman 268—see there; and therefore all who did not immerse—one combines them specifically for zimun of three; but in Yoreh Deah where there is mention of the Name one should be stringent.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.10:_: (10) There but a complete convert they invite zimun on him, etc.—and so above siman 153 seif 19; and see in our words there ot 73.
kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.11:_: (11) There and he may bless birkat hamazon, etc.—even to discharge others. So is in Beit Yosef; and so Razah ot 4.

levushei-serad/part-001.txt.1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 2—and as written in Yoreh Deah siman 268 seif 2—so it should read.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.2:_: Taz s.k. 2—and it is difficult how R' Yitzchak interprets the Mishnah that women, etc.—so it should read.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.3:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 5—and nevertheless they must understand birkat hamazon. For zimun is lighter than birkat hamazon—for obligation in zimun is not so strong as their obligation in birkat hamazon, because some say women in zimun are reshut even when eating with men.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.4:_: Shulchan Aruch seif 8—Androgynous because he is a distinct creature, therefore with his kind; however he invites zimun, not so tumtum—for perhaps this is male and this is female.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.5:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 7—and further in seif 2—meaning in siman 186 seif 2; and if it were that from the Torah she fulfills through the language of one who blesses—the son to his father that he fulfills at least from the Torah—and as in siman 193 see there Taz s.k. 2.
levushei-serad/part-001.txt.6:_: Taz s.k. 2—and this is proven in the chapter ma she-hayah—it appears he was challenged that still what does he want in chapter ma she-hayah; if she discharges others—that is our Mishnah that she does not bless on the cup of zimun; therefore he explained that in the Talmud it deals where there is no zimun; and incidentally Taz explained the dispute of R' Yitzchak and R' Meir; and afterward he wrote and above, etc.—it is another answer to the difficulty how R' Yitzchak interprets the Mishnah that women, etc.

machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:א: (s.k. 1) Am ha'aretz complete—in the Gemara, etc.—he comes to settle the word complete that implies there is am ha'aretz who is not complete. And if he does not recite Keriat Shema—they do not invite zimun on him (Shach)—for Sefer HaGuf wrote the reason they invite zimun on am ha'aretz is they rely on this tanna who said what is am ha'aretz—all who does not recite Keriat Shema morning and evening; and since most am ha'aretz of ours recite Keriat Shema, therefore they invite zimun from them. And the reason he wrote: if an am ha'aretz is found who does not recite Keriat Shema they do not invite zimun—for there is no tanna to rely on to invite zimun on him. And for the reason of R' Yitzchak—meaning the reason Magen Avraham wrote R' Yitzchak said: if we did not invite zimun on them they would separate from the congregation, etc.—there is no distinction in am ha'aretz; and even if he does not recite Keriat Shema this reason applies and they invite zimun on him—this is the view of Kenesset HaGedolah.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:ב: And for an individual we do not care—even if he separates from the congregation.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.2:א: (s.k. 2) And did not immerse—as written in Yoreh Deah siman 124 seif 2—all who did not immerse properly as the law brought in Yoreh Deah siman 268 forbids wine by his touch in drinking—behold he is not yet called Israel; and the same for zimun.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.2:ב: For he is no worse than am ha'aretz in Talmudic times—except that now they invite zimun on am ha'aretz so he not separate from the congregation entirely, as written in s.k. 1; and these, if not for this, would separate.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.4:_: (s.k. 4) Because of, etc.—and therefore even if there are three women, etc.—he comes to settle the scriptural verse that even with fit men women do not combine for zimun, as written at the head of this seif; and therefore he wrote practical difference: if there are three slaves, one need not combine women—for with fit men it is permitted and with slaves forbidden.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.5:א: (s.k. 5) Even though, etc.—and nevertheless they must understand birkat hamazon, etc.—Levush. He comes to settle the difficulty of Levush who challenged on what Rama wrote even though they do not understand—for Rabbenu Yonah wrote siman 193: when two eat and one does not know Hebrew to bless—the knower blesses and discharges the non-knower; and specifically when the non-knower understands lashon kodesh; and Rama did not distinguish from him. Therefore Levush answered what he wrote in siman 193—meaning he understands birkat hamazon. And what Rama wrote here even though they do not understand—meaning they do not understand berachat zimun; but in birkat hamazon they understand.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.5:ב: And Levush wrote the majority, etc.—and meaning he disagrees with Rama who wrote even though they do not understand. And this he brought from responsum of Rosh who wrote women fulfill through hearing birkat hamazon of men; and it is Rama's view—even though it is not women's way to understand lashon kodesh, nevertheless even if they do not understand they fulfill.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.5:ג: And therefore Levush wrote it is not so; rather Rosh's reason is stam women understand somewhat; but if they do not understand at all—in truth they do not fulfill; and as Magen Avraham wrote siman 193 s.k. 1. And in Sefer Avraham Razal he wrote Levush's reason who distinguishes between birkat hamazon and berachat zimun—for in birkat hamazon one need not understand, for we rely on poskim that women in zimun are reshut; therefore in combination one may rely on poskim that one need not understand; and see further there what he wrote.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.6:א: (s.k. 6) The toddlers about nine or ten—I saw incidentally in Sefer Shulchan Aruch with Ba'er Heitev Chadash who wrote: the toddlers as about six or seven; and Magen Avraham wrote about nine or ten—perhaps it is a printing error—until here. And in my humble opinion it is not a printing error; certainly everywhere toddlers were mentioned its measure is six and seven years; but here since Rabbi Yosef Karo wrote in the name of Rif that Tur wrote in his name that the measure of minor is nine or ten—on this Rabbi Yosef Karo wrote—it appears not precise—for behold Rambam wrote seven and eight years and it does not imply they disagree; but certainly any child who knows to whom they bless—they invite zimun on him—and that is one who reached the season of toddlers, i.e., seven and eight years, etc.; but I found for Rashba who wrote per Rif's view ten and nine years—it appears because that is the time of his education. And therefore also seven and eight that Rambam mentioned is because of time of education; but less than this, etc.—they do not invite zimun on him.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.6:ב: And so Rivash in responsa that even per those who permit, etc.—and that he be nine or ten years old or at least older than six, etc.—until here Rabbi Yosef Karo. And since there are disputing views—and Rashba also wrote so is Rif's view that specifically nine and ten—Magen Avraham was stringent and requires nine and ten; and he did not write in language of dispute of poskim, since it is possible Rabbi Yosef Karo also admits we require nine and ten; and so is Rama's way where it is possible the Mechaber also holds thus even if not true—and the Mechaber disagrees; nevertheless Rama did not write in language of some say when known—all the more here it is possible Rabbi Yosef Karo also holds thus that nine and ten are required; and his stam words—for everything is per the sharpness of the child.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.6:ג: Whether for three or for ten—meaning even though for if one ate vegetable to combine for three it was not permitted except one ate vegetable; but to combine for ten—even three vegetable eaters combine with seven who ate bread, as written siman 197—for a minor there is no distinction.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.6:ד: Since for him he exempted himself—meaning his obligation is great—for him he exempted himself; therefore we require specifically an adult for combination.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:א: (s.k. 7) We establish him, etc.—meaning one need not, etc.—do not err in what Rama wrote we establish him as an adult who brought two hairs—meaning his law is like an adult who brought two hairs; and even if we know he did not bring two hairs he combines—on this Magen Avraham wrote; rather meaning in stam we establish him on a presumption that he brought two hairs—for granted for d'rabbanan we rely on presumption that most thirteen-year-olds bring two hairs.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:ב: Before thirteen it does not help—for they are mere presumption.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:ג: And in Yeshuot Yaakov, etc.—therefore we rely on presumption—for it is per his view a rabbinic matter—and it requires study, etc.—since they ruled the doubt stringently—meaning the doubt was for them on daf 20 folio 2 whether women are obligated in birkat hamazon from the Torah or d'rabbanan; and practical difference: if they discharge men—if from the Torah they discharge; and if d'rabbanan they do not discharge—for d'rabbanan does not come and discharge d'oraisa (for women are not in the category of arevut so much the Rosh); and he wrote above siman 186: since they are a doubt whether they discharge men. And if this regarding a minor whose obligation is not from the Torah—cannot discharge an adult except d'rabbanan—the same for a woman: even if not obligated from the Torah, what does not discharge a man is d'rabbanan; and since this question was not resolved—it should go to leniency that they discharge—for it is a doubt d'rabbanan.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:ד: And further in seif 2 there in siman 186 and so in the Gemara—for it asks from this that we taught a son blesses for his father—even though the son is minor and obligated only d'rabbanan, nevertheless he discharges his father who is obligated from the Torah. And it answers the father did not eat to satiety—for also the father is not obligated except d'rabbanan since he does not know, etc.—for they require that the son discharge him even if both know—the mitzvah to separate.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:ה: As written siman 193—two who ate—it is a mitzvah to separate; and even so if one of them does not know to bless—the knower blesses and discharges the non-knower—behold we push aside a rabbinic mitzvah they said mitzvah to separate so the non-knower not be idle from birkat hamazon. And for a minor arevut is not applicable. And as explained in Sotah 41 per the count that he calculated there regarding arevut—therefore minors were not in the category of arevut—see there.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.7:ו: In Milchamot part 3—on the above doubt whether women in birkat hamazon are obligated from the Torah.
